podcast.title: John Hughes Film Exposure (1980s)
podcast.body: General Public's music was frequently included on the carefully curated soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s films. These soundtracks were crucial in introducing a vast number of North American audiences to various alternative rock artists, particularly those from Britain. "So many people learned of bands like The Specials and Spandovalet and Billy Idle and General Public and Wang Chung and Yellow and New Order and the Psychedelic Furs and the Smiths and Echo and the Bunyman, Susanne Vagan in excess the Jesus and Mary chain, Flesh for Luluo and so many others from those soundtrack albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rolling Stone Cover (Fall 1977)
xref.body: The Sex Pistols appeared on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine in the fall of 1977. This issue was one of their poorest selling ever, indicating the general public's resistance to punk rock in North America at the time. "When the sex pistols appeared on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine in the fall of 1977, it was one of their poorest selling issues ever."

xref.title: Early Career Slogging (2009-2015)
xref.body: For six years prior to their mainstream breakthrough with the *Blurryface* album in 2015, 21 Pilots experienced "really hard slogging" during which they were largely unknown to the general public. Despite building a dedicated indie fanbase, they continued to play smaller venues. "But before that, we're six years of really hard slogging when almost no one knew who they were."

xref.body: The Specials were one of many bands whose music was heavily mined for the soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s films. These carefully curated soundtracks played a significant role in introducing a wide audience in North America to bands from the alternative rock scene, particularly British performers. "So many people learned of bands like The Specials and Spandovalet and Billy Idle and General Public and Wang Chung and Yellow and New Order and the Psychedelic Furs and the Smiths and Echo and the Bunyman, Susanne Vagan in excess the Jesus and Mary chain, Flesh for Luluo and so many others from those soundtrack albums."

xref.title: Public Perception and Authenticity
xref.body: The Darkness's distinctive high-pitched vocal style (often mistaken for falsetto) and overall sound led to a divided public opinion, with roughly half of listeners perceiving them as a "bizarre novelty act" and the other half recognizing their genuine artistry. "I think if you survey the general public the results might be about 50-50."
